Simulate epidemic spread for one time step

Source: R/simulate_outbreak_step.R
simulate_outbreak_step.Rd

Simulated epidemic spread for a single time step. This function is documented so it can be used by other packages. However, it is not intended for direct use by users. Please refer to [simulated_outbreak()] for the user-facing version. If you are using this function as part of a separate package, pay attention to inputs as they are not validated. This functions is intended to be used inside a for loop, with input validation being done beforehand.

Usage

simulate_outbreak_step(t, labels, S, I, date_infection, C, tau, w)

Arguments

t

A single integer indicating the current time step. The function will return the state of the epidemic at time t + 1.

labels

A character vector of length n containing the labels of the individuals.

S

A logical vector of length n indicating which individuals are susceptible.

I

A logical vector of length n indicating which individuals are infectious.

date_infection

An integer vector of length n indicating the dates of infection of infected individuals. Entries for non-infected individuals should be -1 by convention.

C

A matrix of size n x n containing the number of contacts or contact intensity between individuals at time t.

tau

A numeric vector of length n containing individual transmission rates.

w

A function calculating the probability mass function of the generation time distribution for given time intervals, as produced by make_pmf_delay.

Value

A list with the following items:

  • $S: same as input, updated.

  • $I: same as input, updated.

  • $date_infection: same as input, updated.

  • $tree: a 3-columns data.frame with columns from, to, and date reporting new transmission events which took place at time t+1

Details

The force of infection (FOI) from individual \(i\) to \(j\) at time \(t\) is defined as:

\(\lambda_{t, i \rightarrow j} = I_{t,i} C_{t, i \rightarrow j} \tau_{t,i} w(t - T_i)\)

The total FOI experienced by individual at time is summed over all possible sources of infection: \(\lambda_{t, \bullet \rightarrow j} = S_{t,j} \sum_i \lambda_{t, i \rightarrow j} \)

It follows that individual \(j\) becomes infected at time \(t+1\) according to a Bernoulli distribution with probability: \( 1 - e^{-\lambda_{t, \bullet \rightarrow j}} \)

To keep track of chains of transmission, the infector of \(j\), denoted \(alpha_j\), is drawn from a Multinomial distribution weighted by the respective FOIs directed towards \(j\): \( \alpha_j \sim \mathcal{M}(1, \lambda_{t, 1 \rightarrow j} / \lambda_{t, \bullet \rightarrow j} ,\lambda_{t, 2 \rightarrow j} / \lambda_{t, \bullet \rightarrow j} , \ldots , \lambda_{t, N \rightarrow j} / \lambda_{t, \bullet \rightarrow j} ) \)
